title: Produce faithful supported product candidates
statement: The system shall derive the supported skill archives, CLI package candidate and architecture browser product resources from canonical authored product sources and declared target transformations, preserving complete intended behavior, required resources, and an accurate supported inventory.

what.problem: A generated package can omit a required resource or silently alter instructions while appearing to represent the authored product.
what.desired_outcome: Users and reviewers can identify a complete candidate whose target adaptations preserve the selected product behavior.

why.rationale: Faithful portable distribution connects authored product meaning to the artifact a user actually obtains.

conditions: When generating a candidate or changing a target transformation or included resource.

contexts: Canonical sources, target descriptors, generated inventory, and actual candidate artifacts.

how.approach: Apply declared inclusion and transformation rules to canonical skills and CLI inputs. Preserve untransformed resource paths and bytes and complete transitive resource coverage. Record exclusions with reasons instead of shipping unsupported dependencies. Derive support manifests in candidate output and keep the selected target population consistent across package metadata and public guidance. Include declared browser generation, profile and reading resources with exact dependency and compatibility information.

how_much.scope: The existing Packaging profile owns exact target roots, archive names, entrypoint rules, projection manifests, and transformation semantics. The selected current direction has Codex and Claude Code targets; old OpenCode evidence is historical, not current install eligibility. This obligation does not introduce a target or claim completed adoption. Browser distribution is an additional proposed product surface whose exact format remains to be designed; it is not another agent target.

acceptance_criteria: The candidate inventory agrees with canonical sources and declared inclusion/transform rules; required mapped and transitive resources are present, and untransformed content retains its skill-relative path and raw bytes.
Declared transformations preserve selected skill behavior; unsupported fields or runtime dependencies reject or have an explicit exclusion reason rather than silently losing behavior.
Generated support manifests agree with the candidate version and actual inventory and do not use a tracked generated manifest as source truth.

Candidates and current guidance agree on the selected supported targets and omit retired target output, wrappers, exclusive resources, and permission-broadening instructions. Historical records are not rewritten.

A browser candidate includes all declared generation, profile and offline-reading resources and licenses; runtime dependencies and supported configurations are explicit. A reference documentation snapshot cannot substitute for the reusable product inventory.
